tags.definition: Adds (or subtracts) the numerators and also the denominators, e.g. 3/4 + 1/4 = 4/8.
Adds or subtracts the numerators of fractions with different denominators without first making the denominators the same, e.g. 2/3 + 1/6 = 3/6.

labels.en: added without making the denominators the same
labels.hi: हर बराबर किए बिना जोड़ दिया

tags.definition: Believes a fraction with a bigger denominator is bigger, e.g. 1/6 > 1/4.

labels.en: thought a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction
labels.hi: सोचा कि बड़ा हर मतलब बड़ी भिन्न
labels.kn: ದೊಡ್ಡ ಛೇದ ಎಂದರೆ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಭಿನ್ನರಾಶಿ ಎಂದು ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದೀರಿ

tags.definition: Compares fractions by looking only at the numerators, e.g. 3/5 > 2/3 because 3 > 2.
Makes an 'equal' fraction by adding or subtracting the same number on top and bottom, e.g. 2/3 = 3/4.

labels.en: added the same number to the top and bottom
labels.hi: ऊपर और नीचे एक ही संख्या जोड़ दी
labels.kn: ಮೇಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಳಗೆ ಒಂದೇ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಕೂಡಿಸಿದ್ದೀರಿ

tags.definition: Changes only the numerator or only the denominator when simplifying or scaling, e.g. 6/8 = 3/8.

labels.en: changed only the top or only the bottom
labels.hi: सिर्फ़ ऊपर या सिर्फ़ नीचे की संख्या बदली
labels.kn: ಮೇಲಿನ ಅಥವಾ ಕೆಳಗಿನ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಬದಲಿಸಿದ್ದೀರಿ

tags.definition: Stops before the simplest form or treats a non-simplest fraction as simplest, e.g. 12/18 = 6/9.

labels.hi: सबसे सरल रूप तक नहीं पहुँचे
labels.kn: ಅತಿ ಸರಳ ರೂಪಕ್ಕೆ ತರುವ ಮೊದಲೇ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ್ದೀರಿ

tags.definition: Multiplies across the diagonal instead of top-times-top and bottom-times-bottom, e.g. 2/3 x 3/4 = 8/9.
Multiplies both numerator and denominator by a whole number, e.g. 3 x 2/5 = 6/15.

labels.en: multiplied both top and bottom by the whole number
labels.hi: पूर्ण संख्या से ऊपर और नीचे दोनों को गुणा कर दिया

tags.definition: Divides by multiplying straight across without flipping the second fraction, e.g. 3/5 ÷ 3/10 = 9/50.

labels.en: divided without flipping the second fraction
labels.hi: दूसरी भिन्न को उलटे बिना भाग किया

tags.definition: Flips the first fraction instead of the second when dividing, e.g. 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 2/1 x 1/4 = 1/2.

labels.en: flipped the first fraction instead of the second
labels.hi: दूसरी की जगह पहली भिन्न को उलट दिया

tags.definition: Chooses the wrong operation for a story problem, e.g. adds 2 + 3/4 when the story needs 2 x 3/4.

labels.en: picked the wrong operation for the story
labels.hi: कहानी के लिए गलत क्रिया चुनी

tags.definition: Uses the right method but makes a small calculation slip.

labels.hi: तरीका सही, हिसाब में छोटी गलती

tags.definition: The mistake could not be identified with confidence.

labels.en: not sure yet, please type your answer
labels.hi: अभी पक्का नहीं, कृपया उत्तर टाइप करें
labels.kn: ಇನ್ನೂ ಖಚಿತವಿಲ್ಲ, ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಟೈಪ್ ಮಾಡಿ

questions.method: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number: 2/3 = (2x2)/(3x2) = 4/6.

questions.stem: 3/5 = ?/10. What number goes in the blank?
questions.method: 5 x 2 = 10, so multiply the top by 2 as well: 3 x 2 = 6.
Multiply the top and bottom by 3: 3/4 = 9/12.

questions.stem: 4/6 = 2/?. What number goes in the blank?
questions.method: 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so divide the bottom by 2 as well: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
Divide the top and bottom by 2: 6/8 = 3/4.
The biggest number that divides 12 and 18 is 6: 12/18 = 2/3.

questions.stem: Which fraction is already in its simplest form?
questions.method: 5 and 7 have no common factor except 1, so 5/7 cannot be simplified.
Divide the top and bottom by 5: 15/25 = 3/5.

questions.stem: What is the lowest common denominator of 1/4 and 1/6?
questions.method: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 6: 6, 12. The first common one is 12.

questions.stem: Rewrite 2/3 and 1/4 with a common denominator.
questions.method: The common denominator is 12: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.

questions.stem: To add 1/2 and 1/5, both need the same denominator. What is the lowest one?
questions.method: Multiples of 2 and 5 meet first at 10: 1/2 = 5/10 and 1/5 = 2/10.

questions.stem: 3/4 = ?/20. What number goes in the blank?
questions.method: 4 x 5 = 20, so multiply the top by 5 as well: 3 x 5 = 15.
Same denominator: add the numerators and keep the denominator: 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3.
Make the denominators the same: 1/2 = 2/4, then 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.
Make the denominators the same: 1/3 = 2/6, then 5/6 - 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.
Same denominator: add the numerators and keep the denominator: 3/5 + 1/5 = 4/5.
Make the denominators the same: 2/3 = 4/6, then 4/6 - 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.
Same numerator: fewer, bigger pieces. A quarter is bigger than a sixth, so 1/4 > 1/6.
Use a common denominator of 15: 3/5 = 9/15 and 2/3 = 10/15, so 2/3 is bigger.
Same numerator: the biggest denominator makes the smallest pieces, so 2/9 is the smallest.
Use a common denominator of 8: 3/4 = 6/8, and 6/8 > 5/8, so 3/4 is bigger.
Top times top and bottom times bottom: (2x3)/(3x4) = 6/12 = 1/2.
Multiply only the numerator by the whole number: 3 x 2/5 = 6/5.
Top times top and bottom times bottom: (1x4)/(2x5) = 4/10 = 2/5.
Multiply only the numerator: 4 x 3/8 = 12/8 = 3/2.
Keep the first, flip the second, multiply: 1/2 x 4/1 = 4/2 = 2.
Keep the first, flip the second, multiply: 3/4 x 2/1 = 6/4 = 3/2.
Keep the first, flip the second, multiply: 2/3 x 9/4 = 18/12 = 3/2.
Keep the first, flip the second, multiply: 5/6 x 12/5 = 60/30 = 2.

questions.stem: Ravi ate 1/4 of a pizza and Meena ate 2/4. How much did they eat together?
questions.method: Together means add: 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 3/4 m long. It is cut into pieces of 1/8 m each. How many pieces?
questions.method: How many 1/8s fit in 3/4 means divide: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 x 8/1 = 6.

questions.stem: Each bag holds 2/3 kg of rice. How much rice is in 6 bags?
questions.method: 6 equal bags means multiply: 6 x 2/3 = 12/3 = 4 kg.

questions.stem: A tank is 5/6 full. Then 1/3 of the tank is used. What fraction of the tank is full now?
questions.method: Used means subtract: 5/6 - 1/3 = 5/6 - 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.
Same denominator: add the numerators and keep the denominator: 3/4 + 1/4 = 4/4 = 1.
Make the denominators the same: 2/3 = 4/6, then 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6.
Keep the first, flip the second, multiply: 3/5 x 10/3 = 30/15 = 2.

questions.stem: A cake needs 3/4 cup of sugar. How much sugar for 2 cakes?
questions.method: 2 equal cakes means multiply: 2 x 3/4 = 6/4 = 3/2 = 1 1/2 cups.
